entries.abstract: We formalize in Lean the principal statistical and constrained-landscape results of Statistical thresholds for Tensor PCA by Jagannath, Lopatto and Miolane, following a local expanded manuscript prepared solely by Patrick Lopatto, the formalization’s maintainer. This elaborated manuscript was prepared to facilitate autoformalization. At nonnegative signal strength in the ordered Gaussian tensor model, we prove the detection threshold below and above criticality for even orders k ≥ 6. For k ≥ 3, we prove the maximum-likelihood value limit at every nonnegative signal strength and the maximum-likelihood absolute-overlap limit away from criticality. We prove optimality bounds for independently randomized measurable unit estimators at nonnegative noncritical strengths, and tensor MMSE formulas at positive noncritical strengths. We also prove the discontinuous overlap transition, consistent testing among fixed nonempty finite families of distinct supercritical strengths, constrained expected and almost-sure energy limits for signed overlaps in [-1,1], and associated variational and landscape conclusions. Almost-sure limits concern fixed parameters and allow arbitrary coupling across dimensions. For interior overlaps, the four-parameter variational reduction establishes equality of infima; unrestricted minimizer attainment is not claimed.
entries.title: Statistical thresholds for Tensor PCA

entries.abstract: This project formalizes the main central limit theorem of “Central limit theorem for the complex eigenvalues of Gaussian random matrices” by Advay Goel, Patrick Lopatto, and Xiaoyu Xie (arXiv:2306.10243v2), using an expanded local manuscript as the detailed proof source. The local manuscript was prepared to ease autoformalization by adding details to the proofs. Its main theorem (Theorem 1.3) is identical to the main theorem of the arXiv version: the hypotheses and conclusion are unchanged. Only this main theorem is advertised.
entries.title: Central limit theorem for the complex eigenvalues of Gaussian random matrices

entries.abstract: Finite quantitative sparse-kernel and necessary expected-row bounds for independently subsampled binary Walsh matrices, with uniform asymptotic and recovery/RIP consequences.
entries.title: Sparse kernels and necessary sampling for binary Walsh matrices

entries.abstract: For every integer q at least 3, the formalization proves the existence of a limiting q-colorability threshold for sparse random graphs. A single constant alpha_q in [1/2, log(q)/log(q/(q-1))] gives the transition for the uniform model with floor(c n) edges and the transition at d = 2 alpha_q for the binomial model with edge probability d/n. For every fixed eta in (0,1), there is C > 0 such that, for all sufficiently large n, the first loss of q-colorability under independent uniform additions of unordered pairs of distinct vertices lies within C n (log n)^(-3/2) steps of deterministic integer centers with probability at least 1-eta. The centers divided by n converge to the same alpha_q. Repeated edges are retained in this process. The scope is Theorems 1.1 and 1.2 of the included manuscript.
entries.title: Existence of the q-colorability threshold for sparse random graphs

entries.abstract: Lean formalization of Schatten-class truncated Toeplitz operator results from the local Lopatto–Rochberg manuscript. Includes analytic and coanalytic Besov classifications for every real p>0, compactness and interpolation criteria, splitting and polynomial-symbol results, and Hilbert–Schmidt energy, differential and squared-kernel quotient descriptions.
entries.title: Schatten-class truncated Toeplitz operators

entries.abstract: Lean 4 formalization of the principal superfluid-stiffness, nonclassical rotational-inertia, winding, and high-temperature normal-phase results of the supplied manuscript, with concrete hard-sphere path measures and Dirichlet-form response definitions.
entries.title: Superfluid stiffness and nonclassical rotational inertia of the dilute hard-sphere Bose gas

entries.abstract: Lean proofs of three-Lambert-series formulas for pi^(4m-1), pi^(4m+1), zeta(4m-1) and zeta(4m+1), for m>=1, together with a separate formula for pi and the signs of the rational denominator coefficients.
entries.title: Odd zeta values and powers of pi

entries.abstract: Lean proves that the finite-complexity affine-linear prime asymptotic implies infinitely many geometric isomorphism classes of rational elliptic curves of each exact Mordell–Weil rank five, six, and seven. The generic analytic theorem is an explicit hypothesis. The specialization checks, two-isogeny descent, exact rank calculations, and passage to infinitely many j-invariants are formalized; the prime asymptotic is not proved in Lean here.
entries.title: Elliptic curves of exact ranks five, six, and seven: conditional formalization

entries.abstract: Lean formalization of the spherical Gaussian spin-glass dynamics and its positive-semidefinite Cugliandolo--Kurchan limit, including the physical variational response, entropy and Fisher estimates, stationary translated clusters, general-spin selection and aging bounds, and stationary relaxation. Theorem 11.4 covers every integer p >= 3 and beta > 0. The cubic product inequality includes beta = beta_d; strictly positive Fisher-cost conclusions require beta > beta_d. The root Challenge retains the original complete-conclusions theorem with the five principal theorem groups and all-spin forward theorem, sharing CK, stationary-profile, dimension-subsequence, density and Fisher-majorant witnesses. The same file separately retains the original Proposition 5.7 statement for every CK solution, every late sequence and every raw translated cluster.
entries.title: Aging in Spherical Spin Glass Dynamics

entries.abstract: A Lean formalization of open phases with every prescribed finite replica symmetry breaking depth in mixed even-spin Ising models at zero external field and positive temperature. The first selected result constructs strictly increasing even degrees beginning at four and a nonempty open set of positive effective covariance coefficients, with an optimizing probability measure having exactly k+1 support points. The independent statement uses concrete Gaussian Cole–Hopf recursions and comparison against all finite schemes at every competing depth. The substantive development constructs minimizers over all probability measures and includes the revised quadratic-inclusive universal transition, exact phase geometry and asymptotics, atomic Hessian, entropy, and analytic comparison results.
entries.title: Replica symmetry breaking at arbitrary depth

entries.abstract: Formalization of a fixed-temperature N^(-7/10) bound for the finite-size mean bias of the zero-field Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model with independent standard Gaussian couplings and the unnormalized partition function. For every beta > 1, a positive constant depending on beta bounds the nonnegative pressure gap for every integer N >= 2. The selected results also establish the thermodynamic limit for beta > 0, the corresponding free-energy-density and expected log-partition corrections, a positive exponent saving over 2/3, and a full-sequence little-o improvement. The independently readable interface defines the limiting pressure by a thermodynamic limit; Solution identifies it with the all-probability-profile Parisi variational value.
entries.title: Finite-size mean bias of the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick free energy

entries.abstract: A Lean development of upper and local lower minimax bounds for nonlinear functionals of conditional means under bounded, rough random design. The generic theorem covers the root-n regime and the subcritical regime with its density-dependent stretched-exponential correction, logarithmic upper and lower factors, and a one-quarter minimax probability lower bound. The substantive development also contains projection, polynomial-estimator, Poisson reduction, lattice-prior, application, and causal-identification results. The selected Comparator surface is the generic theorem's two parts. The remaining logarithmic gap is unresolved.
entries.title: Nearly Minimax Rates for Functional Estimation Under Rough Random Design

entries.abstract: Minimax root-mean-square bounds for estimating a constant conditional variance from independent random-design regression observations. The design density has fixed positive lower and upper bounds but no smoothness; covariate-dependent errors have uniformly bounded conditional fourth moments. For 1 < s < d/4, the proved bracket identifies the polynomial exponent 2(s+1)/(d+4) and the common explicit stretched-exponential factor, with a remaining logarithmic gap. It also proves the exponent corollary, the exact low-smoothness rate, and the parametric regime.
entries.title: Nearly minimax variance estimation under rough random design

entries.abstract: Lean formalization of Patrick Lopatto's zero-field Sherrington–Kirkpatrick results. The selected claims are full interval support, a nonnegative smooth density with a terminal atom for every inverse temperature beta > 1, and quantitative inequalities for that actual atom. The independent Challenge defines the Parisi functional through concrete bounded-gradient weak PDE solutions, with terminal log cosh and coefficient beta squared divided by two. Solution identifies that definition with the constructed Parisi potential. The repository retains the supporting PDE, diffusion, covariance, minimizer, and numbered-result development described in COVERAGE.md and results.json.
entries.title: Full replica symmetry breaking in the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model

entries.abstract: A Lean formalization of the positive-field Sherrington–Kirkpatrick results in Patrick Lopatto's arXiv:2604.11921v2. The selected registry claims are convergence of the expected finite-volume free energy to the concrete replica-symmetric Gaussian formula for beta > 0, h > 0, and AT parameter at most one, including equality; and an exact description of the positive-field AT boundary as a positive strictly increasing smooth graph on beta > 1, tending to zero at beta = 1 from the right, together with (1,0). The repository also contains the numbered PDE, stochastic-process, moment, and variational results documented in COVERAGE.md and results.json.
entries.title: Replica symmetry up to the de Almeida–Thouless line in the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model
